title: Red Chilaquiles with Fried Eggs

qty.unit: tortillas, torn in pieces — stale ones are the point

qty.note: split between the tortillas and the eggs

qty.unit: medium (half in the salsa, half in rings)

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, chipotle, garlic, and half the onion into a rough salsa — a few pulses, not a puree.
Cook the salsa with half the salt in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes, until it darkens and smells roasted rather than tinny.
Meanwhile, heat 3 tbsp oil in the second skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Fry the tortilla pieces in two batches, 5-6 minutes total, stirring so both sides crisp. Drain on a paper towel.
Take the salsa off the heat and fold the crisped tortillas through it — off the heat they drink sauce without going soft. The pieces should still offer some crunch.
Fry the eggs in the last of the oil over medium heat until the whites are fully set but the yolk still moves. Eggs are safe at 160°F (71°C) on a thermometer — check one if your pan runs cool.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Divide the chilaquiles among plates. Lay an egg on each, then drizzle the crema and crumble the queso fresco over everything.
Finish with the raw onion rings and cilantro, and eat at once — chilaquiles wait for no one.

cuisine_note: Chilaquiles is what Mexican kitchens do with yesterday's tortillas: fry them crisp, drown them in red salsa just long enough, and crown them with whatever the fridge offers. Stale tortillas fry up better than fresh.
